utterances.text: So in terms of sequence, we're always the same day now. Then 21.57.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Then 22.30.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And now we have 21.48?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, to me, looking -- if I'm looking at this book, it would indicate to me there was a change of date here. To you, I guess, it's not the case.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Let's go on. The next one is 22.47?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the next one is 8.11.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, is that a change of date to you?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So then we would now be on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on. 8.26.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: 14.45, if you can indicate that with a pencil.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Then 14.46. Then 15.03.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmmm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you indicate that.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Then 20.25.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Then 21.37.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Then 21.44.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And now we have 18.48.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, to me, that would indicate a change of date.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. I mean, I -- I see it's a three-hour difference, but it's possible that this conversation was left behind. I would keep going through the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So there's a -- you will admit that there's a possibility, given a three-hour gap.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not when you go to the next page and you see that it's the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Then we go next to 7.02.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: This would be the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. So to me, in that sequence, from the 19 of July until the 21 of July, I see two possibilities for someone - I'm not talking about you, who has spent hours and hours looking at these books; I'm talking of the Trial Chamber - trying to look at the book and to see whether, by the sequence of events, I can establish just by looking at the book that the dates are correct. I'm talking about the date of 21 of July, at 7.02. Because to me, looking at it, my -- the result, I suggest to you, is I come to 23 July.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what's your question? Can I take this off --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will try to make this easier. To me there were two changes of dates that took place based on the sequence of the conversations. And one happened when we had from 22.30 until 21.48, and you said that this was not -- this did not indicate a change of day.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And then there was a second one, which was from 21.50 until 18.48, and I thought that was a change of date and you said it didn't -- it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I don't have the book, I cannot say that; is that -- that's my question. If I don't have the book and the information to corroborate this, I'm not able to, looking at the notebook, to establish a date.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the notebook, I think it is possible. If you just look at loose pages unrelated and you can't -- you don't -- you can't put them all together, then I would say no, you couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't -- I don't seem to have the transcript on the screen, and I'm pushing the buttons but it's not happening. Oh, there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Maybe just to assist the Court here, I have an example I can -- with this exact intercept, and I'm looking at the transcript and that was on page 5446 of the transcript, where we had the intercept operator who was here, and the intercept operator basically testified, and I will quote for you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Give us the date, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The date is on 12 December 2006, transcript page 5446, and that was at lines 15 to 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And then it's the exact case where we say that the conversation was recorded at 14.25, and then the question was: "Are we still talking about the 17th of July? And if we take the first intercepted conversation written down at 13.18," the question was: "So it is logical to say that this conversation took place the day after, on the 18th of July." The answer was: "Logical, yes, looking at this notebook." Now, that's the intercept [sic] who took this conversation. But I'll move on to another topic. That was just at least to provide a reference, unless you want to add something.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess I just lost you a little bit. I thought -- you said 5446 -- I'm sorry, I went to the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, sorry, 5446 was a transcript page of a witness who testified, so you cannot find it before you.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So I was just providing a reference for the sake of the Trial Chamber of the intercept operator who took this conversation and who testified to that effect.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, based on the work --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Maybe she wishes to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I invited comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She's still reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: She's unable to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: She's cannot read the [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, she's reading what you dictated or what you read. Do you wish to comment on that or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't have anything to change about what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Bourgon, your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Based on the work I did comparing the notebooks with the printout headers, I found out, at least from someone looking at the notebooks and the headers, I found many differences and many questionable results. Would you be surprised if I show you examples where the date in the header does not correspond in the printout, does not correspond with walking through, by changing dates every time there's a change in the time?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would have to show me examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to our first example, which was the exhibit P1422A, that was the first intercept I showed you today.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you give me an ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will put it on the screen for you. An ERN? 1422.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 1224B, maybe?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry, 1224, yes. And I'm looking now at 1224, if I can have C, for Charlie. Sorry, it's there. I was still on the ELMO. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. On the right side of your screen, do you see the conversation at 1622 hours, and that is 255 -- the frequency 255850.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The date that is indicated in the header, you will agree with me, is 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, my question is simply, I've worked out the dates in the notebook and I came in -- I came -- my result was four different possibilities, and three of the four possibilities were that the conversation was not on the 17th of July. Would you agree with me that because of the way the notebooks are made, that's quite possible?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Why is this?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the reasons that I've explained; that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you answer, I think she needs to know the three or four possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- before she can give a reasoned answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When we looked at the book together, and let's go back to the ELMO and the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can we have the ELMO and -- sorry, it's me. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I look at this book and I see on the left page here, page 1460, I see the date "14th of July, 1995." I look at the page beside, on the right, and I see on page 1461, to me there's a very -- by looking at it, that this conversation started at the same day that this book is, which is on the 14th of July. Is that a possibility for me, looking at this book?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you don't know what you're looking at, it's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's all I'm asking for.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And -- but given the fact that we've looked at many of these books and we went through, because it wasn't also clear to us whether the date, for example -- in this example, the 14th of July, was something that could be relied upon. And a couple of times we've talked about the fact that for -- that those were internal numbers and dates that were recorded by the commander, and that those dates didn't bear -- that we -- didn't bear -- that they weren't related to the dates that were in the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I don't deny that. You've explained that before.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can move on, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm just saying that this is a possibility for me looking at this book, that the first conversation was on that date, and I need to look further.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: You need to know more in order to be able to have an accurate assessment of what you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's exactly what my question is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, we are through with it, and I think the witness understood the question and she answered it. Why don't we move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'll move on to my next area of questions, and that deals with the authentification binder. That was P1074. And my first question is something that I believe -- I'm not sure if you did say it in your testimony, but to analyse the intercept was a long and labourious process. You'll agree with that?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in that binder, which you called --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I have the transcript up again?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- authentification binder or autentikesen [phoen], you have produced 12 instances where one or more intercepts have been compared with other information.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you stated before in your testimony that this was a sample.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Those two -- those 12 instances were a sample.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I imagine that if you wanted to testify before this Court, you picked some very good samples; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We tried to pick samples that were broad and representative and covered dates, yes, a variety of dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I imagine that even though this is a sample, that you did the same type of exercise with many more intercepts.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with some. I don't have a firm recollection of how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But is it, like 50, 100, or 1.000?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Less than 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Because today you mentioned in your testimony that just for the month of July - and I was surprised by this information so maybe I'm wrong, but I'm just trying to -- you said that just for the month of July you were dealing with 1.200 to 1.800 conversations. Was that -- is that what you -- is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, using sample methodology, my next question is simply: Did you ask anyone, an expert in the statistics field, in order to be able to conclude on the reliability or the authenticity of 1.800 intercepts for July, how many you would have to look at to have a mathematical representative sample.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I object. I don't think the witness has testified that she employed a sample methodology with respect to the preparation of the authentication binder that my learned colleague is inquiring about. Moreover, I don't think it's been sufficiently defined on the record in order to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She -- she -- she's answered "to an extent," but this is a -- somewhat of a different question. Let me consult with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need to move, Mr. Vanderpuye and Mr. Bourgon. The question basically is one which the witness needs to answer: Was the sample methodology -- it's being suggested to you that the sample methodology used was not a sufficient one, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Maybe I can rephrase the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can rephrase it in whatever way you like, but let's move. I mean, it's a fair question, of course, but let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When you say that the authentification binder represents a sample, which you've said on a number of occasions, are you referring to sample methodology under mathematical sample methodology, or simply it's a sample and no more than a sample?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The latter. It's a sample.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And my understanding of the purpose of the authentication binder is that if I look at those 12 examples, this should be enough to convince me that all intercepts are authenticated. Is that the purpose of the binder?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think those 12 samples have to be looked at with the other processes that we employed in authenticating and determining the reliability of the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I understand, Ms. Frease, that you went through a very elaborate process, but my question is: If I'm looking at the intercepts, my question to you is, I need more information for every single intercept in order to determine whether the intercept is authentic or not.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with the statement, but I'm not sure that it's my position to agree or disagree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. I simply suggest to you that for any particular intercept, unless I have more information, as was the case to establish the date, unless I have more information, I cannot conclude that it is authentic and reliable.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take a few examples to see if we can maybe be more precise. Let's take in the authentification binder and let's look at tab 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's possible to have the binder given to the witness or to -- because ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have a copy that I can provide, Mr. Bourgon, if you'd like to inspect it before I hand it up to the witness, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Just give her tab 2. For me that's fine, because we're -- I just want to do this intercept and then I'll have a few more questions when we resume on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I can accommodate that, the tab 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to see it, Mr. Bourgon, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I don't, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I look under tab 2 and I would just ask some questions to confirm whether my understanding of the binder is the right one. Now, under tab 2, you have five different intercepted conversations, and the topic is that there would be a Serbian flag that would be flying on the church in Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: In terms of authentification material or corroborating material, depending on the term you use, and I turn now to -- I'm looking at the page 0092, where it says "Corroborating Material," you have two pictures; a picture of 11 July 1995, where it says "Two still photographs that show a Serbian flag on the Orthodox church in Srebrenica." And they were taken from a video that was shot on 11 July.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And then you have also as corroborating material two pictures that date from a video shot on 13 July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I simply suggest to you that the corroborating material that you have here, these pictures, do not allow you to draw any conclusions concerning the reliability of the conversations or the five intercepts, that is, the wording of the intercepts, other than the topic of a Serbian flag. That's my -- that's what I suggest to you.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And why do you suggest that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, maybe we'll be more precise. Let's take the first intercept. Is there anything in the first intercept, on page 0085 -- and I look at those pictures, and, to me, I'm not able, from the pictures, to confirm the wording of that conversation.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have a very poor photograph of the -- of the -- I have a very poor copy of the photograph. But what's indicated in the intercept is that there is "a Serbian flag on the ruined Orthodox church in Srebrenica." And I believe that the two photographs, one might have been a close-up; one might have been taken a bit further away, to show that it was on the church in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Let me make my question more precise. Let's move to the next intercept on page 0087. And we see here that this intercept is between someone called Stankovic and an unidentified man.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anything in those pictures that you are providing as corroborating material that allows you to confirm that the intercept operator actually heard Stankovic?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intercepted conversation indicates that the conversation was recorded between a man named Stankovic and an unidentified man, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm simply asking, from the picture, which is your corroborating material, are you able to say that Stankovic was speaking in this intercept?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the photograph, no, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's -- that's --

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the content of the intercept indicates that Stankovic is saying that there is a Serbian flag on the Serbian church in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So the topic of the conversation goes with the topic of the intercepts.

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's what you're -- that's the only conclusion you can draw from tab 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that it was made on the 11th of -- that it was recorded on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you cannot conclude whether the identity of the people speaking or the exact words that they used by making a comparison between the two?

utterances.speaker: STEFANIE FREASE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. She has answered the question the negative, in any case. Do you still want to object?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Only to the line of inquiry because I think it's been gone over many times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I don't think, Mr. President, it's been -- gone over time. But we are finished for today. Now, Mr. President, I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has adjourned the sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, I will ask you to adjourn, but I have a difficulty that I need to address with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can send Ms. Frease to enjoy the well-merited weekend. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The difficulty I have is that I need about 20 minutes to finish with the witness. Unfortunately, I'm -- I cannot be here on Monday. I would ask the leave of the Court to be able to conclude my cross-examination, if need be, after my colleagues on Tuesday. If the witness is gone by then, then I guess I will just have to not finish my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then what?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And then on the basis of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no, because you're saying -- you're assuming that your colleagues will take the entirety of Monday's sitting, which would make possible for you, then, on Tuesday to continue and finish off your cross-examination. But if we finish all the other cross-examinations on Monday and you haven't cross-examined the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My preferred option, Mr. President, is to hand my questions over to someone else to ask them on my behalf, because I cannot be here on Monday. Now, what -- the situation we are in is that we -- it's very difficult for us to plan ahead, given the constant changes in the witness schedule. We keep changing schedules. The Prosecution always changes. And for us, if I plan a day away for investigation purposes - that cannot be changed - then I'm in trouble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's stick to one point. What's going to happen if, on Monday, we finish the cross-examination, all the other cross-examinations. You're not here and you still have questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If, I believe, I can show a good case, show good cause, I would ask for the witness to be called back. She works here in the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually, she doesn't work in the building, and my understanding is that there may actually be a complication with respect to her availability into next week. I'm going to try and ascertain the extent of it. My understanding right now is there may actually be a problem with her presence being secured for Tuesday and beyond, but obviously I can't have contact with her so I'm going to try to ascertain the extent of her availability through the victims' services unit. But her availability is not -- is not as simple to obtain as Mr. Bourgon might otherwise think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can't you prepare the questions and hand them over to -- to your lead counsel, who is --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We'll do, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Very well. More than capable to handle that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We'll do to make it easier for everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Have a nice weekend. We'll resume on Monday morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
